1	# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai-4B Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)
2	
3	Primary model: models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (572 MB, arch qwen3, 36 layers,
4	embd 2560, GQA with 1024-wide K/V projections, 253 MUL_MAT nodes per token
5	= 36 x 7 + lm_head).
6	
7	Why 4B (decision 2026-07-21, replaces the old 27B focus):
8	- Fits andesim hybrid's hard 2 GiB guest-RAM cap with room for KV cache and
9	  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB
10	  DRAM support).
11	- Plain qwen3: output is coherent on rv64. The qwen35 hybrid-attention bug
12	  (old F0) only affects 27B, so it no longer blocks anything - parked below.
13	- The full closed loop already works on 4B: end-to-end cycle-accurate
14	  per-kernel measurement under andesim hybrid marker mode was confirmed
15	  2026-07-16 (see Measurement setup).
16	
17	Hardware targets (both vsim engines, VLEN 512-2048 family per F4 design):
18	- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
19	- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.
20	
21	Baselines:
22	- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
23	  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.
24	- Real cycles, hybrid marker ROI at K=51 (layer 7 V projection, 2560x1024,
25	  the smallest matmul in the model - nothing smaller exists per-layer):
26	  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
27	  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)
28	  These are THE per-kernel before/after gate for F1-F7: same K, same model,
29	  real pipeline + memory system.
30	
31	Rules for every feature below:
32	- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
33	  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
34	  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
35	- Benchmark gate: QEMU proxy for correctness + rough insn counts, then
36	  hybrid marker ROI cycles before/after (the real number). FPGA only for
37	  final full-token figures.
38	
39	ELEN=32 constraint (ax45mpv_premium): no 64-bit vector elements anywhere.
40	Stock repack.cpp uses __riscv_vsseg4e64 -> GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF today; any
41	new F4 kernel must stay e32-clean (the Nx1 design already is: vlm masks,
42	int16 sumi, fp32 accumulators). Also: premium's FP datapath rejects LMUL=8
43	float ops (integer LMUL=8 is fine) - F4's VLEN=512 -> m4 fp32 mapping is
44	exactly at the safe limit; never use m8 for float.
45	
46	Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE / PARKED
47	
48	---
49	
50	## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)
51	
52	- Status: TODO
53	- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
54	  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
55	  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
56	  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
57	- Gate: K=51 ROI cycles before/after (V projection is exactly this path).
58	- Key files:
59	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-578 (vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher)
60	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:227-232 (.nrows field of GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)
61	- Dependencies: none. Small diff, big win - good first step if F4 stalls.
62	
63	## F2. Q1_0 defer reductions - REMOVED
64	
65	- Status: REMOVED (2026-07-22, user decision). The vl512/vl512w candidate
66	  kernels were deleted from kernel-lab/ (q1_0.c/h, test harness); the lab
67	  dispatcher routes VLEN >= 256 to vl256 again. Rationale: it removed the
68	  per-group scalar stall but kept the horizontal reduction and the 32-lane
69	  fill, so it could never be more than a modest win; F4 (row-parallel
70	  repack) solves the actual problem and makes this path dead weight.
71	  Lesson kept for the record: QEMU TCG charges per vector instruction and
72	  makes scalar ops ~free, so this kind of stall-removal restructure READS
73	  AS A REGRESSION under QEMU (n=8192: vl256 57.5us vs vl512 75.5us) -
74	  never judge restructures by QEMU; only vsim/FPGA cycles count.
75	
76	## F3. Q1_0 full-VLEN utilization - FOLDED INTO F1/F4
77	
78	- Status: folded (2026-07-16 finding) - because Q8_0 activations are NOT
79	  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
80	  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
81	  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
82	  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.
83	
84	## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)
85	
86	- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-22) - F4a DONE, F4b lab-verified pending
87	  cycle gate; largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
88	- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
89	  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
90	  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
91	  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
92	    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
93	    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
94	    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
95	    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
96	  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
97	    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
98	    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
99	    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
100	    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
101	    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
102	- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
103	  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
104	  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
105	    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
106	  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
107	- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
108	  ```
109	  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
110	  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
111	      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
112	      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
113	      for c in 0..31:
114	          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
115	          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
116	          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes

# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai-4B Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)

Primary model: models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (572 MB, arch qwen3, 36 layers,
embd 2560, GQA with 1024-wide K/V projections, 253 MUL_MAT nodes per token
= 36 x 7 + lm_head).

Why 4B (decision 2026-07-21, replaces the old 27B focus):
- Fits andesim hybrid's hard 2 GiB guest-RAM cap with room for KV cache and
  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB
  DRAM support).
- Plain qwen3: output is coherent on rv64. The qwen35 hybrid-attention bug
  (old F0) only affects 27B, so it no longer blocks anything - parked below.
- The full closed loop already works on 4B: end-to-end cycle-accurate
  per-kernel measurement under andesim hybrid marker mode was confirmed
  2026-07-16 (see Measurement setup).

Hardware targets (both vsim engines, VLEN 512-2048 family per F4 design):
- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.

Baselines:
- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.
- Real cycles, hybrid marker ROI at K=51 (layer 7 V projection, 2560x1024,
  the smallest matmul in the model - nothing smaller exists per-layer):
  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)
  These are THE per-kernel before/after gate for F1-F7: same K, same model,
  real pipeline + memory system.

Rules for every feature below:
- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
- Benchmark gate: QEMU proxy for correctness + rough insn counts, then
  hybrid marker ROI cycles before/after (the real number). FPGA only for
  final full-token figures.

ELEN=32 constraint (ax45mpv_premium): no 64-bit vector elements anywhere.
Stock repack.cpp uses __riscv_vsseg4e64 -> GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF today; any
new F4 kernel must stay e32-clean (the Nx1 design already is: vlm masks,
int16 sumi, fp32 accumulators). Also: premium's FP datapath rejects LMUL=8
float ops (integer LMUL=8 is fine) - F4's VLEN=512 -> m4 fp32 mapping is
exactly at the safe limit; never use m8 for float.

Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE / PARKED

---

## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)

- Status: TODO
- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
- Gate: K=51 ROI cycles before/after (V projection is exactly this path).
- Key files:
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-578 (vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:227-232 (.nrows field of GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)
- Dependencies: none. Small diff, big win - good first step if F4 stalls.

## F2. Q1_0 defer reductions - REMOVED

- Status: REMOVED (2026-07-22, user decision). The vl512/vl512w candidate
  kernels were deleted from kernel-lab/ (q1_0.c/h, test harness); the lab
  dispatcher routes VLEN >= 256 to vl256 again. Rationale: it removed the
  per-group scalar stall but kept the horizontal reduction and the 32-lane
  fill, so it could never be more than a modest win; F4 (row-parallel
  repack) solves the actual problem and makes this path dead weight.
  Lesson kept for the record: QEMU TCG charges per vector instruction and
  makes scalar ops ~free, so this kind of stall-removal restructure READS
  AS A REGRESSION under QEMU (n=8192: vl256 57.5us vs vl512 75.5us) -
  never judge restructures by QEMU; only vsim/FPGA cycles count.

## F3. Q1_0 full-VLEN utilization - FOLDED INTO F1/F4

- Status: folded (2026-07-16 finding) - because Q8_0 activations are NOT
  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.

## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)

- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-22) - F4a DONE, F4b lab-verified pending
  cycle gate; largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
  ```
  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
      for c in 0..31:
          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
  ```
  ~3 ops/col (1 vlm + vsub_vx + vadd_vx_m), all N-wide; ~393 N-wide ops per
  block-tile => ~6 ops/row/block at N=64 vs ~20 for single-row vec_dot, AND
  full VLMAX, AND no reduction stalls. Per-column vlm (128/block) is the
  main tuning point. Everything is e8/e16/e32 - ELEN=32-clean by design.
- N and LMUL mapping: fix N=64, adapt LMUL to vlenb at runtime so the fp32
  accumulator is full: VLEN=2048->m1, 1024->m2 (fpga_l3), 512->m4 (premium,
  FP-LMUL limit respected). One repacked type; nc must be a multiple of
  N=64 (2560 and 1024 both are; machinery handles remainder).
- Sub-features (do in order):
  * F4a - DONE (2026-07-22, kernel-lab): `repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64x1` +
    `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0_generic` (keeps the reference float-op order) +
    test_repack_gemv: bit-exact vs per-row vec_dot_generic on the original
    data, shapes up to nr=192/n=1024, random + 0x00/0xFF edges. TDD:
    zero-stub RED first, then GREEN.
  * F4b - lab kernels DONE, cycle gate PENDING (2026-07-22): vl512
    (i16m2/f32m4, premium FP-LMUL max) + vl1024 (i16m1/f32m2) + vlenb
    dispatcher in kernel-lab/q1_0.c. Scale expand via integer bit math
    (lab_expand_fp16_64_*) - no zfh/zvfh needed, premium-safe. Correctness:
    double-ref gate PASS at VLEN 512/1024 (max_norm_err 2.7e-06), generic
    path at 256/128. Generated asm clean: 3-insn column loop (vlm + vsub.vx
    + masked vadd.vx), no spills. QEMU --bench proxy on K=51 shape
    (2560x1024): 0.73x vs per-row vec_dot - EXPECTED artifact (TCG helper
    cost on masked ops/vlm; same lesson as removed F2, do NOT tune to it).
    MEASURED on RTL (2026-07-23, standalone rdcycle shootout at
    vsim-demo/q1_0, nr=64 x n=512, warm, results match on both):
      fpga_l3      VLEN=1024:  vl256  829 cyc/row -> gemv 125 cyc/row = 6.6x
      premium_full VLEN=512 :  vl256 1044 cyc/row -> gemv 174 cyc/row = 6.0x
      (M=1 premium_full-era record; the CANONICAL M=4 table with the new
      engines premium_max + HVM placement is in F4c below)
    Extrapolated K=51 (2560x1024, 8 blocks/row): fpga_l3 4.2M -> ~0.64M,
    premium ~5.3M -> ~0.9M; ~5-6x on the matmul portion of the ROI.
    Engine note: plain sim_ax45mpv_premium is built from a NDS_FELEN=0
    config (NO vector FP - every vf* traps); the VLEN=512+FP engine is
    sim_ax45mpv_premium_full (added to vsim_andesim config.yaml 2026-07-23,
    premium RTL + data/configs/ax45mpv_premium_full.cfg, FELEN=32 = fp32
    vector only, enough for zve32f). Its probe passes ALL vector-FP ops
    including vfwcvt.f.x.v - the vsext+vfcvt split in the kernel is
    optional there (kept: portable, ~free).
    Engine specs (from the cfg files):
      sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3     : VLEN/DLEN 1024, FELEN 64, L1 32K/32K,
                                L2 DISABLED (0), L3 2MB enabled
      sim_ax45mpv_premium_full: VLEN/DLEN 512, FELEN 32, L1 64K I$/8K D$,
                                L2 32KB enabled, no L3; ILM 1MB/DLM 32KB
    The 8KB D$ on premium (< lab warm set ~15KB) means its warm reps lean
    on L2; fpga_l3 warm reps are L1-resident.
    Remaining gate: K=51 marker ROI after F4d wiring.
  * F4c - gemm (M>1 prefill) - lab kernel DONE + MEASURED (2026-07-23,
    vsim-demo/q1_0 `q1_0_gemm_64x1`, nr=64 x n=512 x M=4, TDD RED->GREEN,
    QEMU ALL PASS at 512/1024, then RTL rdcycle, warm rep, ALL PASS):
      CANONICAL (engines = fpga_l3 + premium_max, cyc/dot warm):
        fpga_l3     1024 tile4: RAM 840/126/40  | HVM 785/92/37
        premium_max  512 tile2: RAM 1045/135/75 | HVM 753/83/54
        (columns = vl256 baseline / gemv x4 / gemm)
      Best chain RAM-baseline -> HVM-gemm: fpga_l3 22.7x, premium_max 19.4x.
      History premium_full (8K D$): RAM 1049/206/109 - D$ was its bottleneck.
    Design: every sign-mask vlm (+ its addressing) is loaded once and shared
    by the whole M-tile; per extra activation only 2 int vector ops + 1
    scalar load. M-tile is register-budgeted: 4 at VLEN=1024
    (sumi m1 x4 + facc/sumf m2 x8 + dx/temp ~ 25 regs), only 2 at VLEN=512
    (f32m4 accumulators, ~29 regs); both compile with ZERO vector spills.
    Amortization tracks tile size: masks shared 4-way -> 3.1x, 2-way -> 1.9x.
    ggml wiring (ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0 interleave + mmid tile loop) is part
    of F4d. Dep: F4b (done).
    HVM A/B (2026-07-23, -DQ1_HVM=1, hvm.h CSR-probe allocator ported
    printf-free from ace-tq1, ALL data in HVM, numbers in canonical table):
      findings - D$ size only helps repack kernels (8K->32K: gemv 206->135)
      and never the vl256 baseline (latency-bound, not capacity-bound);
      HVM ignores D$ size entirely (premium_full HVM == premium_max HVM)
      and still beats 32K D$ on the vlm stream (83 vs 135); HVM reps are
      deterministic (rep0==rep1). K=51 fit: premium 256KB HVM holds a
      64-row strip (~22KB); fpga_l3 8MB holds the whole 2560x1024 repacked
      weight (360KB) -- room for ~22 such weights (in-model: 22 attn_v land
      in HVM, the rest overflow back to RAM).
    premium_max engine (2026-07-23): premium RTL re-elaborated with ELEN=64
      FELEN=64 PACKED_FP16=yes D$ 8K->32K (ax45mpv_premium_max.cfg) -
      builds, probe_max (rv64gcv) 15/15 ok incl. e64 + f64 + zvfh-encoded
      f16->f32. Premium was never hard-limited to ELEN32; config knobs.
  * F4d - ggml wiring DONE (2026-07-23, TDD RED->GREEN), K=51 gate PENDING:
    block_q1_0x64 + repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64_bl + generic gemv/gemm (bit-exact
    vs vec_dot order) in repack.cpp; RVV kernels (runtime vlenb dispatch:
    m1/m2 @VLEN>=1024 tile4, m2/m4 @512 tile2, vlm +-y hot loop, integer
    fp16 expand, vsext+vfcvt) in arch/riscv/repack.cpp; traits instance +
    dispatch (Q1_0 + riscv_v + VLEN>=512 + ne1%64==0); arch-fallback aliases
    for all non-riscv arches. Fixed the stock e64 blocker (quantize_mat_
    q8_0_4x8's RVV body now needs __riscv_v, zve32f falls to generic) and
    un-gated quantize_mat_t<1,Q8_0> from zvfh (generic 4x1 otherwise).
    NEW TEST tests/test-repack-q1_0.cpp (extra-buft mul_mat vs default-buft
    reference; test-backend-ops skips CPU-only so it cannot see repack):
    RED = zero-stub 3/3 FAIL nmse=1.0; GREEN = 3/3 OK nmse=0 (bit-exact) at
    QEMU VLEN=512 AND 1024 (rv64gcv build); x86 host = clean SKIP.
    Build note: repack path needs march WITH v/zve32f - build-rv64 now
    configured -march=rv64gcv -mext-zvlsseg (ELEN=64 decision, premium_max).
    K=51 MEASURED on fpga_l3 (2026-07-24, andesim hybrid marker, Bonsai-4B,
    same cmdline as baseline): 4,476,168 -> 2,144,755 cycles = 2.09x on the
    whole MUL_MAT node. Gap vs lab 6.6x is expected: in-model the 2560x1024
    weights (360KB repacked) stream from L3 (L1 32K only),
    activation quantize is scalar generic (no zvfh build), plus node
    overheads; the lab strip was L1-resident.
    WEIGHTS-IN-HVM DONE (2026-07-25, same K=51 ROI; committed q1_0-rvv-opt
    510479ad8): ggml-cpu/hvm.h + repack set_tensor redirect, gated by env
    GGML_Q1_HVM or -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v (off by default). At load the
    selected Q1_0 repack tensors are written straight into HVM (0x90000000;
    fpga_l3's 8MB window holds 22 attn_v weights, the bump allocator overflows
    the rest back to RAM), so the per-column sign-plane stream reads banked
    local memory, not L3. K=51 blk.7.attn_v is in HVM ([roi] print confirms
    src0). HEADLINE: baseline (pristine vec_dot, weights in L3/cache)
    4,476,168 -> optimized (repack row-parallel kernel + weights in HVM)
    946,460 = 4.73x end-to-end. Breakdown: repack kernel alone (both in RAM)
    2.09x, then HVM alone (same kernel, RAM->HVM) a further 2.27x.
    CORRECTNESS VERIFIED bit-exact: HVM-on vs no-HVM
    binaries (both VLEN 1024, greedy) produce byte-identical output
    ("...Paris. Paris is the capital of France...") -- the win is on a correct
    kernel, not a broken one. Verified through a new andesim capability: fast
    mode now accepts a vsim engine and -readconfig's its HVM geometry, so the
    whole model runs functionally under HVM with no cycle leg (andesim
    feat(run) 5f039b5). Remaining levers: activation quantize RVV (e32-clean),
    M>1 prefill tiles, F6 ACE.
    ROI-counter fix included: MUL_MAT counting moved BEFORE the extra-buffer
    dispatch in ggml_compute_forward (repacked matmuls return early there;

    premium_max K=51 BLOCKED on vsim_andesim: ax45 subsystem hybrid resume

- Status: TODO

  to hide the L3/DRAM miss latency that makes the repacked kernel load-bound.

  behind the `GGML_RV_ZICBOP` CMake option (off by default), and without it
  `__builtin_prefetch` compiles to a nop. Build must pass `-DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON`

  further only adds MSHR/cache pressure.

  per-32 vwredsum reduction):

  stalls on L3/DRAM misses).

The Andes toolchain (`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc`, GCC 14.2, target `riscv64-linux`) does NOT enable RVV tuple segment load/store intrinsics (`__riscv_vlseg*`, `__riscv_vsseg*`, tuple `vcreate`/`vget`) with plain `-march=rv64gcv`. They are gated behind Andes-specific machine flags:

- `-mext-zvlsseg` - segment load/store
- `-mext-zvlss` - strided load/store
- `-mext-zvlsidx` - indexed load/store

**Why:** Andes vector units make these instruction groups optional, so the fork hides the intrinsics unless the flag is given. Errors look like "implicit declaration of __riscv_vlseg2e32_v_u32mf2x2", which wrongly suggests the intrinsics are missing.

**How to apply:** When an intrinsic is "not declared" under this toolchain, first check `riscv64-linux-gcc --target-help | grep -i <feature>` for a `-mext-*` flag. Do not rewrite the source. For llama.cpp rv64 builds, pass `-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg`. Working cross-build configure (build dir `build-rv64`):

```
cmake -B build-rv64 \
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$TC/riscv64-linux-gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$TC/riscv64-linux-g++ \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-mext-zvlsseg \
  -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 prefetch reproduce
# runbook (q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md): pristine / baseline / prefetch (+ optional hvm).
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   hvm      = repack + weights-in-HVM (older experiment, now superseded)
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh prefetch           # just the shipped kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 (see q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md shape table):
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK      : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON    : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                            gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N   : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
#   -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME     : HVM redirect selector; only on the HVM build
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack toggle   $3 extra defines (DIST / HVM selector, or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | hvm
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    hvm)      cfg "$LLAMA/b-hvm$SUF"      "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME=attn_v" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|hvm|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

for t in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do build_one "$t"; done

Yes - `opt_roadmap.md` F6 (lines 284-348) is the ACE-RVV item, still TODO. But while checking it I found something that changes the answer: **your target RTL already has Andes vendor dot-product instructions, so you may not need custom ACE at all.**

## 1. What F6 in the roadmap says

Three candidates, A recommended:

| | insn | shape | new HW |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `v_q1_rowdot` | 4-way sign-dot, lanes = rows, no reduction, pairs with the F4 Nx1 repack | most |
| B | `v_q1_unpack` | bits -> +-1 int8, then reuse `v_w_mul_free_macc` | least |
| C | `v_q1_sign_macc` | single-row, still needs the per-32 `vwredsum` tail | mid |

It was written before F4/F7 landed, and it assumed you must build the instruction yourself with COPILOT.

## 2. New facts (checked just now, not from memory)

- `/local/nick/vsim/data/configs/ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg` ISA string already contains `xandesvdot1p0 xandesvqmac1p0 xandessintload1p0 xandesvpackfph1p0`. `NDS_VECTOR_VDOT_SUPPORT = yes` on **all three** engines (premium, premium_full, fpga_l3).
- The Andes GCC 14.2 assembler knows these already: `nds.vd4dots.vv` (+ `.vv u`/`su`), `nds.vqmacc.*`, `nds.vln8.v` (load nibbles -> int8), `nds.vle4.v`, `nds.vfwcvt.f.b.v` (byte -> float, one op), `nds.vfpmadb/t.vf` (packed fp16 MAC). I compiled and disassembled one: `1388445b nds.vd4dots.vv v8,v16,v24`.
- **No intrinsics** in GCC 14.2 (`__riscv_nds_vd4dots_*` = implicit declaration). Inline asm only.
- Not verified: whether QEMU executes `nds.vd4dots` (you stopped me mid-test), and the exact operand semantics. Both need one small run before committing.

So F6 splits into: **B-stock** (use `nds.vd4dots`, zero new hardware, works today) vs **A-custom** (COPILOT + RTL, 1-bit weight native).

## 3. How much is actually left to win

From your own measured points on K=51 / fpga_l3:

| build | cycles | |
|---|---|---|
| pristine | 4,476,168 | 1.00x |
| repack (F4) | 2,144,213 | 2.09x |
| repack + prefetch (F7) | 1,391,650 | 3.22x |
| repack + HVM (weights in local RAM) | 946,460 | 4.73x |

The HVM number is the same kernel with memory stalls removed, so it is close to a pure-compute floor. Today's 1.39M is roughly **68% compute, 32% memory**. ACE / vdot only attacks the compute part:
- absolute ceiling if compute became free: ~0.45M (3.1x more)
- realistic (3-4x fewer hot-loop ops): ~0.6-0.75M, so **about 1.8-2.3x**

## 4. What vdot changes in the kernel

Now, per column per 64-row tile (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1789-1794`): `vlm` + `vsub.vx` + masked `vadd.vx` = 3 vector ops, and the two ALU ops form a **serial loop-carried chain** on `sumi`.

With `nds.vd4dots`, per **4 columns**: `vlm` + `vmerge` (bits -> +-1 int8) + activation splat + `vd4dots` = 4 ops.
- ~3x fewer vector ops
- chain becomes 1 op per 4 columns instead of 8 -> **8x shorter dependency chain**
- accumulator is i32, so `vsext.vf2` disappears
- cost: the repacked sign bits must be reordered (4 columns per row byte-lane instead of column-major planes). That is a load-time change, free at run time.

## 5. Cheaper first (pure RVV, no new HW, same bottleneck)

11.5 cycles per column-tile even in HVM, for 3 instructions, says you are **latency-chain bound, not throughput bound**. Two software fixes attack exactly that:

1. **bsums trick** (same one in your ace-tq1 notes): drop the per-column `vsub`. Sum the 32 activation values once as a scalar, do only the masked `vadd` per column, subtract `sum_y` once per group. 3 ops -> 2 ops per column, chain 2 -> 1. No overflow risk (max 8128 in int16).
2. **Split accumulators**: 2-4 independent `sumi` registers over interleaved columns, add them at group end. Breaks the loop-carried chain. Registers are free at i16m1/VLEN=1024.

Both are hours of work in `kernel-lab/` with the existing rdcycle flow. If they land most of the win, the vdot upside shrinks a lot - so measure them first.

## 6. Recommended order

1. bsums + split accumulator (pure RVV, ships everywhere, cheapest)
2. `nds.vd4dots` prototype in kernel-lab, inline asm, A/B on vsim (no RTL work needed)
3. LM head repack gate (rows%64 = 53 fails, ~26% of a decode pass) - bigger than both, and not ACE
4. Custom ACE (real F6-A) only if 2 shows the +-1 form clearly beats int8 vdot

Roadmap is stale on two points: it treats `xandesvdot` as "stock but unexamined", and F6 still says "awaiting user pick of A/B/C". Want me to update F6 with these findings?

CC:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

# Toolchain DEFAULT runtime + -mvh (Andes virtual hosting): no custom
# crt0/libgloss/handler. The same ELF runs on Andes QEMU and on vsim.
# No zfh/zvfh in march: premium has neither; fp16 scales are expanded with
# integer vector ops (fp32 math needs zve32f).
CFLAGS:= -march=rv$(XLEN)gc_zve32f -mvh -O2 -ffp-contract=off -fno-tree-vectorize

# engines (use the vsim_andesim builds - RAM to 0x8fffffff, sim_control OK)
# premium_full = premium RTL + FELEN=64 config; the plain premium build has
# NDS_FELEN=0 (no vector FP - every vf* traps), do not use it for this kernel
SIM_PREMIUM ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium_full
SIM_FPGA_L3 ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3
# premium RTL reparameterized to ELEN=64/FELEN=64/packed-FP16/32K D$
SIM_PREMIUM_MAX ?= /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium_max

# vsim flavor: same sources, linked with the vsim BSP (sim_control MMIO I/O);
# vsim does not service -mvh virtual-hosting syscalls, QEMU does not model
# the sim_control device - hence one flavor per runner.
VSIM_LINK := $(VSIM_FILES) $(VSIM_FLAGS) $(VSIM_OPTIMIZE)

all: test_q1_0 test_q1_0_v1024 test_q1_0_vsim test_q1_0_vsim_v1024 test_q1_0.dump

	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(CFLAGS)

# gemv built for VLEN=1024 (i16m1/f32m2) - run on sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3.
# Our objects avoid 'c' (ax46mpv has Zcmp, not Zcd: compressed FP stores are
# illegal there); prelinked libc is rv64gc, so stay on integer-only printf
# (iprintf) to keep libc's float-printf (which has c.fsdsp) out of the link.
